clue.text: What may be covered by parts of ITV

definitions.text: What may be covered by parts of ITV

blocks.clueFragment: What may be covered by parts of ITV
blocks.note: surface reading: something reported on by some of ITV's programmes
setter's reading: ITV is a commercial channel, and its programmes come in parts separated by advertising slots

explanation.walkthrough: ITV is Britain's main commercial television channel; its programmes are split into parts, and what falls between the parts is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval for advertisements on television sits between segments of a programme, filling the gaps between its parts.

clue.text: Former dancer not in a televised broadcast

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter seed widely, so the letters are strewn about and resown in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A retired dancer laments never having appeared on a TV transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: Ninette de Valois founded the Royal Ballet; 'broadcast' looks like part of the TV picture but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: She was an Irish-born ballerina and choreographer, founder of the Royal Ballet, who died in 2001.

clue.text: What one hopes may win sweepstake is not designed for motoring!

definitions.text: What one hopes may win sweepstake

blocks.clueFragment: What one hopes may win sweepstake
blocks.note: first reading: in a Grand National sweepstake each entrant is allotted a runner at random, and hopes that runner wins
second reading: pulled by an animal rather than powered by an engine

explanation.surface: A sweepstake fancy turns out to be a vehicle hopeless on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as two words: the runner you drew in the office sweepstake.
explanation.definitionFit: A carriage or cart pulled by animals predates the car and is plainly not built for motor traffic.

clue.text: Obliquely request to take over from one leading the waltz?

indicators.note: taking over from someone means stepping into their place, so one piece ousts another letter

blocks.note: to request is to ask
the waltz is a dance, whose leading letter is D
a waltz is a kind of dance

explanation.surface: A dancer asks, sideways, to cut in and take over leading the waltz.
explanation.walkthrough: ASK replaces the D at the front of DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking askance means glancing sideways, so the word works as an adverb for indirectly or with suspicion.

clue.text: Not all of tummy fits in? It could be a warning!

indicators.note: not all of something means part is missing, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: tummy is a homely word for the belly

explanation.surface: Someone whose tummy won't squeeze into their clothes takes it as a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: BELLY loses its last letter; 'fits in' is padding saying the shortened word fits the four squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells are rung as alarms, for fire, for ships in fog, or at level crossings, so one can be a warning.

clue.text: Second thoughts about not supporting team that needs helping

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
con means against, as in pros and cons
a team is a side
a helping is a portion or ration

explanation.surface: A manager has doubts about backing a struggling team that needs help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' looks like a verb about aid but is the noun, a share of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking a matter over again, perhaps changing one's mind, is having second thoughts about it.

clue.text: Former CND enthusiast transformed duller ranters and the leaders of British socialism

indicators.note: leaders come at the front, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept
transformed means changed in shape, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written for the rearrangement
the initials of these two words

explanation.surface: A peace campaigner turned tedious left-wing orators into something better.
explanation.walkthrough: CND is the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, the British anti-nuclear movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The philosopher was the first president of the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament and a lifelong pacifist activist.

clue.text: Game suffices for keeping order at home

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one word is held within another

blocks.note: 'that does' means that suffices
OM is the Order of Merit
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A board game is enough to keep the household in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' suggests tidiness at home, but it is the Order of Merit, an honour; the two short pieces split the verb after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The pastime is played with small oblong tiles marked with pips, matched end to end.

clue.text: French student issued with name and number

blocks.note: élève is French for a pupil
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A French pupil is handed a name and a registration number.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is a cardinal numeral, the figure after ten, so it is a number.

clue.text: French town gets a second look in

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the pair of letters around it

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
mien is a person's look or bearing

explanation.surface: A French town is given a second look by visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: MIEN goes between A and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiens is a cathedral city in Picardy, northern France, capital of the Somme department.

clue.text: A world of sweets?

blocks.note: surface reading: a whole universe of confectionery
setter's reading: a world holds every kind of thing, and the sweets in question are named for their variety

explanation.walkthrough: Liquorice Allsorts are a British mixed bag of liquorice sweets; the name means every variety.
explanation.definitionFit: These liquorice confections come in many shapes and colours, a varied assortment of candies in one packet.

clue.text: Sand in bottle

blocks.note: first meaning: small loose particles of stone
second meaning: British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.surface: Sand inside a glass bottle, as in a seaside souvenir.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, bottle is nerve: to lose your bottle is to lose your courage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fine gravelly particles and determined courage in the face of difficulty.

clue.text: Squalid sink transformed with a nice bit of disinfectant

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters are rebuilt in another order
a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here just its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A filthy sink is made over with a nice squirt of disinfectant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squalid' looks like a description of the sink, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens wrote of poverty and slum conditions, so the adjective describes grim, filthy Victorian squalor.

clue.text: The foreign wine town showing ability to increase accommodation

blocks.note: el is 'the' in Spanish
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A wine town in Spain shows it can expand its hotel capacity.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretchiness is the capacity to expand and give room, as a waistband stretches to accommodate more.

clue.text: Witty person holding in measure of sound? He's not witty!

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so the witty person's letters go round the rest

blocks.note: a wag is a joker
taken as written
dB is the decibel, a unit of loudness

explanation.surface: A joker measuring noise contrasts with someone who has no wit at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter reuses wit on purpose: the wordplay starts from a joker, while the definition says the result is the opposite of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tedious talker full of empty chatter is the opposite of a witty speaker, so he is not witty.

clue.text: Frank Field's central character in French story!

indicators.note: a central character stands in the middle, so only the middle letter of the word is used

blocks.note: frank means candid
the middle letter of the five-letter word

explanation.surface: Frank Field, the MP, plays the lead in a French tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank Field was a British Labour MP; his name hides the adjective frank. Voltaire's Candide is the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaire's satirical novella of 1759 follows its naive hero through misfortune, a celebrated tale from France.

clue.text: Eat ice-cream, swallowing whole

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: a cone is an ice-cream cornet
the sum is the whole amount

explanation.surface: Eat the ice-cream cornet whole, gulping it down.
explanation.definitionFit: To devour food is to take it in; consuming and eating are synonyms.

clue.text: Fool admits nothing to right-wing organisation - a devilish sign?

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the fool's letters enclose the rest

blocks.note: coot is a dated word for a fool, as in 'silly old coot'
love is nil in tennis
NF is the National Front, a British far-right party

explanation.surface: A fool lets nobody into a far-right group, a sign of the devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing' is tennis scoring, where zero is called love; the enclosed pieces sit after the fool's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is traditionally pictured with split hooves like a goat's, so a cloven hoof marks the Devil.

clue.text: Defeat with tail-ender finally dismissed

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter of the word is used

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
a dismissed batsman is out

explanation.surface: A cricket side loses once its last batsman is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: A tail-ender is a weak late batsman in cricket; here the word just supplies its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing defeat; as a verb it means to defeat decisively and put to flight.

clue.text: Note about marriage guidance counsellors supplied by clergy

indicators.note: about means around, so the note wraps round the counsellors

blocks.note: a PS, postscript, is a note added to a letter
Relate is the British relationship counselling charity

explanation.surface: Clergymen provide couples' counselling, along with a note.
explanation.walkthrough: Relate, formerly the Marriage Guidance Council, is a British charity offering couples counselling.
explanation.definitionFit: Prelates are senior churchmen such as bishops, so collectively they are members of the clergy.

clue.text: Office worker's degrees in abbreviated form?

blocks.note: first meaning: a temporary secretary or clerk
second meaning: the short form of temperature, measured in degrees

explanation.surface: An office worker's qualifications are listed in shortened form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degrees' suggests a worker's qualifications, but it means the readings on a thermometer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an agency stand-in at a desk and the standard shortening of temperature.

clue.text: Copper shown by examination to be most clever

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: A policeman's exam results show him to be the brightest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute can mean shrewd or sharp-witted, as in 'a cute move', so its superlative means cleverest.

clue.text: Is male following unhappy perversion?

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the earlier pieces are placed behind the later one

blocks.note: unhappy means sad
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Is a man pursuing someone miserable showing a kink?
explanation.definitionFit: Deriving pleasure from inflicting pain on others is classed as a sexual deviation.

clue.text: Being this could mean mum losing energy, just!

definitions.note: points at the answer as a state one may be in: being matronly

indicators.note: losing something means it goes missing, so one letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: mater is Latin, and old public-school slang, for mother
E is the symbol for energy
just means only

explanation.surface: A mother running low on energy only just manages to be a matron.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opening phrase, 'Being this', so the rest reads as: being matronly could mean a mum minus energy plus just; mater is old slang for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Matronly describes a dignified, motherly, middle-aged woman, the state the opening phrase asks you to name.
